\section[el equipaje]{el equipaje — the luggage}

\label{lesson:ES-C478-equipaje}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to earn, then the Spanish for three hundred.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el equipaje}
\textbf{el equipaje} — \textquotedblleft{}the luggage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El equipaje de mano no puede pesar más de diez kilos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hand luggage cannot weigh more than ten kilos.}
\end{quote}

It is singular, like English luggage: \emph{mi equipaje}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el equipaje}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el equipaje}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el equipaje}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to earn, then the Spanish for three hundred, then say \emph{el equipaje} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el equipaje mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The luggage\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\label{lesson:ES-C478-calzado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for three hundred, then the Spanish for the luggage.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el calzado}
\textbf{el calzado} — \textquotedblleft{}the footwear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Wear comfortable footwear.}
\end{quote}

A notice word for shoes in general; one shoe is \emph{un zapato}.

Before the new one: say the Spanish for the luggage, then the Spanish for the footwear.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el sitio}
\textbf{el sitio} — \textquotedblleft{}the place; the room, the space\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\emph{Un sitio web} is a website.

\section[el espacio]{el espacio — the space}

\label{lesson:ES-C478-espacio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the footwear, then the Spanish for the place.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el espacio}
\textbf{el espacio} — \textquotedblleft{}the space\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The space is small but it has light.}
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{sitio}, and the word for outer space too.

\section[disponible]{disponible — available}

\label{lesson:ES-C478-disponible}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the place, then the Spanish for the space.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: disponible}
\textbf{disponible} — \textquotedblleft{}available\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La habitación está disponible desde el lunes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The room is available from Monday.}
\end{quote}

Used with \emph{estar}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
